summary: Module 3 REFLECT capture. (1) Reproduction approach: chose B (synthetic reproduction) at DECIDE. Confirmed correct for this fork -- production replay assumed the canonical analytics bucket schema that the checkpoint fork does not have; synthetic allowed building a deterministic interleave repro (forced-identical candidate) that reproduced the same duplicate-key failure class on links.code, and later a deterministic cache-race repro. Same choice again: deterministic synthetic beats flaky replay for race windows. (2) Minimal reproduction quality: repro scripts control exactly one variable each -- repro_race.py varies only concurrency (10 simultaneous redirects, no auth/data/retries); repro_code_race.py forces only the RNG to a constant, changing one variable to make the window deterministic; repro_cache_race.py fixes the interleaving order explicitly. Everything else is ordinary, freshly created data. A teammate can run each script with no explanation and observe the same failure/success. (3) Takeaway: 'A loud error tells you where to look; silent corruption hides the damage until the decision you made on bad data is already public -- so a clean error log is never proof the bug is gone.' Shipped: upsert-equivalent atomic create_link (retry-on-IntegrityError), version-token atomic cache populate/invalidate, three reproduction scripts reusable as CI regression tests.
